title: Aakar Template Families v1 (Avatars)
description: The catalogue of outcome categories. A family is the form a customer's idea takes: a carrier (Avatar) that fuses the idea with an everyday object, one of the parametric object families, or the single raw print family. Seeded from packages/design-tokens/families.json, stored in template_families / shelves / hardware_items, edited in the management portal. Code ids stay snake_case English; brand names (codename, name, tagline) are data.

allowed.description: Digital material ids allowed for this family; null means every available material.

content_slot.description: The Chhaap: what personal content a family accepts and where. A template's features_supported must be a subset of accepts.

anchors.description: Anchor ids the consumer UI offers first.

hero_volume.description: True when the family carries a customer's own 3D form (hero_mesh) in a volume anchor.

id.description: Equals `family` in design specs and template descriptors.

codename.description: Brand name shown to customers, e.g. 'Saathi'. Portal-editable.

name.description: Plain descriptor always shown with the codename, e.g. 'Keychain & bag charm'.

kind.description: carrier = an Avatar that carries the customer's idea; object = a parametric object family (PLAN §7.3); raw = the single 'print as it is' family.

tier.description: Roadmap slot from the market research; `available` is the staff switch.

shelf.description: Shop shelf (catalog category) this family sits on.

default_template_id.description: Template used when a request names only the family.

environment.description: Default viewer backdrop before a template is chosen: an environment id from the reference data (experience.v1.json environments; the API checks it against the environments table).

hardware.description: Bought-in parts packed with every piece; a template descriptor's hardware overrides this default.

shape_tolerance.description: any: a plate or plinth absorbs whatever shape the content has; constrained: content must satisfy a rule (attachment region, flat top, shell); strict: the functional body is parametric and content only decorates it.
